newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRENCH AGF SHARES BOOSTED BY SWISS MERGER.
newsitem.headline: FRENCH AGF SHARES BOOSTED BY SWISS MERGER.

text.p: Shares in French insurer AGF got a lift on Tuesday, after Monday's merger news between Swiss banking giant Credit Suisse and insurer Winterthur Group reopened talk about consolidation in the French financial sector, traders said.
Trading in Assurance Generale de France shares was also boosted ahead of the release of its first half turnover, due after the market closed on Tuesday.
Analysts said the market was discounting flat sales, especially in the life assurance sector.
At 1230 GMT, AGF shares were up 1.13 percent at 214.4 francs after hitting a high for the day of 216.9. The blue-chip CAC 40 index was up 9.3 percent at 2,992.77.

One fund manager said Natwest had calculated that, based on the multiples used in the Swiss deal, AGF shares would be worth 260 francs while insurer AXA would be worth 450 francs. Axa shares were trading at 415 francs, up 0.53 percent, at 1233 GMT.
Analysts welcomed the Swiss merger but were sceptical about the concept of bancassurance, pointing to the French example of insurer GAN and its CIC bank group CIFC.PAagfp.

"This (Swiss merger) has reopened speculation on restructuring in the sector, but I have my doubts whether we will see a systematic concentration in bancassurance," said Philippe Foulquier of brokerage Cholet Dupont.
He had a target of 230 francs for AGF shares at the end of the year, and recommended the stock as a buy. He forecast flat first half figures.

On Friday, financial daily L'Agefi forecast a fall of eight percent in life assurance in the second quarter after a drop of two percent in the first quarter. The daily based these calculations on figures from the French Federation of Insurers.
